newsitem.title: JAPAN: Lloyd's Japan aiming to develop long-term business.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's Japan aiming to develop long-term business.

text.p: The Lloyd's of London insurance market is seeking long-term business opportunities in Japan through the development of new products rather than quick profits, Lloyd's chairman Sir David Rowland said on Tuesday.

Rowland told a news conference marking the formal launch of its Japanese offshoot Lloyd's Japan Inc that Lloyd's did not intend to compete aggressively with Japanese non-life insurers but would emphasise the development of new types of coverage and services.

Lloyd's Japan Inc president Kunihiko Sasamoto told the same news conference that the company would seek to develop such products as earthquake insurance for corporations and tailor-made niche products for corporations.
Rowland declined to forecast the size of insurance business at Lloyd's Japan in the initial year.
The emphasis will be on commercial risk and Lloyd's would not underwrite business at uneconomic rates, he said.
Lloyd's was able to set up the Japanese firm under revised insurance laws which took effect last April. The firm was established last September but formally began business on Tuesday.

"I hope that over a period of time, our office in Japan will be treated as a market, a place where brokers can go to discuss the risk with an underwriter, obtain a quotation and actually place the business with him," he said.
He also said that the launch was timely because the reforms had also allowed insurance broking business here.

Lloyd's has obtained licences to engage in various non-life insurance businesses in Japan, the first overseas management base it has set up its 300-year history. For more than 100 years, Lloyd's has been providing reinsurance services for many of Japan's non-life insurance companies.
Sasamoto said that Lloyd's Japan will try to establish business relations with international brokers in the initial stage, rather than soliciting corporate customers directly.
